companies.evidence_user_adoption: Moderate-to-strong for legacy DTECH/GATR lines (RECALL); F-35 training repeat orders confirmed 2025-2026. MEDIUM.
companies.evidence_repeat_procurement: F-35 P5 IS follow-on (Nov 2025 then May 2026) - HIGH; tactical kit reorders not captured this session.
companies.evidence_prototype_to_production: Halo remains AFRL-funded R&D (no production evidence); DTECH/GATR are mature production lines. MEDIUM.
companies.tech_stack_inference_from_jobs: INFERENCE (no careers search this session): embedded networking (Cisco/Linux), RF/antenna engineering, and for Pixia large-scale imagery services (Java/C++, cloud); RECALL, LOW.
companies.confidence_notes: Corporate structure after 2021: HIGH for Veritas/Evergreen privatization, LOW for any 2024-2026 rebrand or sale (fetch blocked). Product portfolio and historical acquisitions: HIGH/MEDIUM from recall plus 2014 Military Aerospace article. Halo AFRL award and DTECH Fusion Trust launch: MEDIUM (Military Embedded Systems company page summary). F-35 P5 awards: HIGH.

(5) Parry Labs - $49M IDIQ customer and product brand names not verified; total funding conflicts ($116M vs $171M). Contract-data rules applied: ceilings and total-potential values are labeled as such and never equated with revenue; pilots/OTAs labeled prototype; SB-AMTI and Golden Dome stages marked uncertain. Founder-relevance: every company in this batch operates under ITAR/cleared-program constraints; Klas (Irish parent with US subsidiary, later acquired by Anduril) is the most instructive precedent for a foreign-founded hardware entrant, but FOCI/ITAR implications need specialist legal review.
